checks.assertion_review: Independent call/host grants, tool intents and context remain bound to their originating tasks; racing assignments/consumers commit only one route and one consumption. Overlapping drafts in the installed host preserve distinct approval questions and follow-up attribution across restart.

Authenticated MCP origin and current store authority deny forged task/conversation/call selectors, wrong bindings, duplicate authentication, expired grants, revoked backing credentials and accepted replay. A grant can only cancel its explicitly configured bound task; expiry is rechecked after acquiring the database lock.

Child termination exercises before/after transaction commit and reply ACK. App business mutation and inbox checkpoint remain atomic. Competing workers preserve one business action; a remote provider that accepted but withheld its receipt is counted independently and is never redispatched after server or snapshot recovery.

Unbound replies stay unassigned until explicit owner assignment; identical replay, reordered completion and consumed events do not move another task. Assignment/consumption rollback leaves no acknowledged partial effect; task/installation cursors retain their binding after restart.

Old facts beyond the initial serialized context projection are recovered with journal source IDs and provenance. Changed authority, expired grant, deleted/missing/expired artifact, another task cursor and snapshot-ahead cursor deny access or return explicit unavailable metadata without artifact bytes or server paths.

Local native voice records a sourced decision, ends its session, restarts the server and continues the original task through the selected eligible SMS/chat path. Sibling task and another-conversation contrast remain unchanged. Actual provider/model and carrier evidence is separately source-labelled.

Signed STOP cancels queued SMS before any provider send, HELP/STOP/START acknowledgements remain provider-owned, and START only permits fresh eligible intent. Cancelled effect replay stays denied through restart and stale duplicate controls cannot replace newer suppression state.

A slow accepted effect returns honest pending within the bounded tool response; dropped MCP response recovers the same receipt. New protected host grants resume the exact retained session and task, catch up the journal and do not create a second logical mutation.

ordinary_default.assertions_reviewed: The same ordinary key creates and communicates in two conversations through MCP and native QUIC, preserves exact receipts after server restart, denies changing a logical request into another conversation, receives independent contact, and recovers an old sourced fact beyond the recent context projection.

Revoked/actually expired regular keys receive HTTP 401 on discovery and receipt replay. Revoked native replay is unauthorized; the public SDK definitely rejects trusted session expiry before sending. Independently valid receiving-route credentials cannot rescue queued origin authority: both revoke and real expiry cancel the queued SMS and zero physical provider requests occur.

All 23 existing communication tools match native regular-credential outcomes: seven positive cases and sixteen known application denials. Foreign conversation/task inspection, foreign cancellation and ceiling widening are denied; closed schemas reject actor/grant selectors and invalid shapes; provider call/chat/session headers cannot authenticate as ordinary identity authority.

Successful resumable file begin/chunks/finalize/read/delete use native receipt parity; received bytes and digest are verified, and foreign/wrong-conversation/deleted reads deny bytes. Ordinary MCP invites/accepts/reads/ends/cancels/rejects audio sessions; public native SDK peers exchange real 160-byte PCMU QUIC datagrams in both directions and retain Friday context in the same conversation afterward.

Missing enrollment cancels dispatch. A reviewed fresh grant permits ordinary SMS only while STOP is absent. STOP cancels queued and new pending work before any physical send; START permits one fresh authorized intent and never revives old cancelled jobs. A duplicate final delivery callback and restart/replay preserve one observed provider send and three cancelled jobs. Stored message acceptance is explicitly distinct from provider delivery.

A separately authenticated operator revokes the agent key, then uses existing protected issuance to obtain a current non-admin same-agent identity key. It reads retained message/task/effect activity and cancels work without borrowing the revoked key. A different operator identity still cannot bypass conversation membership. The replacement key cannot continue the original revoked task effect. This is an owner-managed CLI/API path, not a new admin history bypass or permission console.

Normal task creation needs only request/conversation IDs and derives current bounded defaults atomically; exact retry returns the same record. Tracked send/reply/wait/cancel work without an invocation grant, a send-only recipient answers a verified question exactly once, wrong question/conversation references and unpaired scope are denied, and task cancellation leaves ordinary conversation messaging usable. Explicit old narrow mode retains its bound schema, step ID and task ceiling and cannot create conversations.

Normal inspection reports current identity/mode/expiry and named tools without plaintext, admin controls or caller identity selectors; revocation denies inspection. Protected identity creation rechecks current admin, preserves one canonical creation on retry and rejects changed/existing intent without state corruption. Read-only install authentication preserves logical state and orphan bytes and observes revoke/real expiry. Default export copies only the selected non-admin agent credential: no operator/provider master secret, task-grant or renewal files; rejected/preexisting installs stay untouched.
